MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.description: Theoretical worst-case modifier stack exceeds 4.0x cap on prep tasks by a wide margin. Expected for exterior trim repaint at extreme conditions.
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_prep: POOR (2.00) x RRP (2.00) x Extreme Height (2.20) x Elaborate (1.60) = 14.08x
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_prep_no_rrp: POOR (2.00) x Extreme Height (2.20) x Elaborate (1.60) = 7.04x
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_coating: QT5 (1.50) x Extreme Height (2.20) x Elaborate (1.60) = 5.28x
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.resolution: STACKING PARTITION — modifiers split into non-overlapping task pools. Extreme combinations flagged for estimator review and T&M recommendation.

prep_tasks.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / (FAC_TRRP_CONDITION x FAC_TRRP_RRP x FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT x FAC_TRRP_COMPLEXITY)
prep_tasks.max_stack: POOR (2.00) x RRP (2.00) x Extreme (2.20) x Elaborate (1.60) = 14.08x
prep_tasks.note: FAC_TRRP_QT does NOT apply to prep tasks. Prep labor is condition-driven, not quality-driven. Extreme stacks represent 19ft+ ornate trim with severe deterioration and lead paint — recommend T&M billing.

coating_tasks.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / (FAC_TRRP_QT x FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT x FAC_TRRP_COMPLEXITY)
coating_tasks.note: FAC_TRRP_CONDITION and FAC_TRRP_RRP do NOT apply to coating tasks. Once prepped, surface is at baseline. 5.28x exceeds 4.0x flag — this is extreme height + ornate + QT5 gloss. Flag for estimator review.

fixed_tasks.note: Assessment, equipment setup, and equipment cleaning are fixed-time tasks. No modifiers applied.

trim_component_input_group.description: Trim tasks consume LF from individual component PS keys. Engine processes each component independently with its own height and complexity modifiers, then sums results. The input_group reference on tasks means the task applies to ALL trim components — the engine iterates over each component's LF.

task_production_rates.name: Condition Assessment — DSD Rating Per Component
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Full condition assessment: DSD rating per component type, ASTM D3359 adhesion test, coating type identification (solvent test), moisture content testing (pin-type meter), rot probe at vulnerable joints (sills, corners, joints). 1.0-2.0 hours per project. Midpoint 90 min. MANDATORY — determines which subsequent modules activate.

task_production_rates.name: ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Adhesion Test
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Cross-hatch adhesion test per ASTM D3359 on existing coating. Minimum 3 test locations per elevation. ~30 min per project. Adhesion failure triggers full prime instead of spot prime.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture Content Testing
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pin-type moisture meter readings at multiple locations per component type. 0.5-1.0 hr per project. Midpoint 40 min. Wood MC must be <15% before priming.

task_production_rates.name: Rot Probe at Vulnerable Joints
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Probe sills, horizontal surfaces, and butt joints with awl for soft rot. ~30 min per project. DSD-4 findings trigger HARD STOP for affected component.

task_production_rates.name: Lead Paint Testing (Pre-1978)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: EPA-recognized lead test kit testing on each component type. Trim is HIGH RISK — historically received oil-based lead paint more frequently than field surfaces. 0.5-1.0 hr per project. Pre-1978 homes only.

task_production_rates.name: Crew Mobilization & Equipment Staging
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mobilize crew, transport materials and equipment to site. Stage paint, primer, prep tools, and protection materials. ~30 min per session.

task_production_rates.name: Scaffold / Lift / Ladder Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Erect scaffold, position aerial lift, or stage extension ladders per access plan. OSHA-compliant setup. ~60 min per session.

task_production_rates.name: Ground & Landscape Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy plastic sheeting and drop cloths at base of work area. Scraping debris containment during prep phase. ~18 sec per SF.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Full coverage with overlap at seams
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full coverage with taped seams, no gaps

factor_modifiers.name: Condition Scale Prep Labor Multiplier
factor_modifiers.description: Universal GOOD/FAIR/POOR condition scale drives prep task production. HARD_STOP triggers scope exclusion.
factor_modifiers.notes: Harmonized from DSD scale. GOOD=1.0x (DSD 0-1 merged). FAIR=1.5x (was DSD-2 at 1.375x, aligned to universal 1.5x). POOR=2.0x (was DSD-3 at 1.75x, aligned to universal 2.0x).

factor_modifiers.name: Lead-Safe RRP Prep Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: EPA Lead-Safe RRP requirements double prep task duration. Adds wet scraping methods, HEPA vacuum between passes, containment maintenance, and lead-safe disposal overhead. Trim is HIGH RISK for lead paint — historically received oil-based lead paint more frequently than field surfaces.
factor_modifiers.gate_condition: IN_BOOL_PRE_1978 = true AND paint disturbance involved
factor_modifiers.notes: Gate condition — binary: either RRP applies or not. 2.00x accounts for wet scraping, HEPA vacuum passes, containment maintenance, and procedural overhead. RRP material costs (poly, HEPA bags, waste bags) are separate consumable items. RRP containment setup/teardown are separate fixed tasks (TSK_TRRP_RRP_CONTAINMENT_SETUP, TSK_TRRP_RRP_CONTAINMENT_TEARDOWN) — NOT modified by this factor.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Rate Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier affects care and rigor on coating tasks. QT3 = baseline (satin). QT4 = greater care (semi-gloss). QT5 = maximum effort (gloss, near-zero defect tolerance).
factor_modifiers.notes: Does NOT apply to prep tasks — prep labor is condition-driven (DSD), not quality-driven. QT3=1.00 baseline, QT4=1.25 (25% slower, tighter tolerances), QT5=1.50 (50% slower, near-zero defect tolerance). Per doctrine key production data.

factor_modifiers.name: Trim-Specific Height Modifier (Per-Component)
factor_modifiers.description: Per-component height tier drives production rate reduction. Trim requires painter AT working height for brush work — no ground-level spray with extension like siding.
factor_modifiers.notes: Uses FAC_TRRP_HEIGHT — NOT FAC_EXT_ACCESS. Trim height tiers (1.30/1.60/1.90/2.20) differ from siding access tiers (1.35/1.60/1.50) because trim requires painter AT working height for brush work. Protection setup/teardown, equipment setup/cleanup, assessment, and RRP containment tasks are NOT height-modified. Per-component assignment: fascia = high/extreme, ground-level casings = baseline.

factor_modifiers.name: Trim Profile Complexity Modifier (Per-Component)
factor_modifiers.description: Profile complexity affects both prep and coating production rates. Per-component — one building may have simple corner boards (1.0x) and elaborate window surrounds (1.60x).
factor_modifiers.notes: Simple flat board (1x4 corner) = baseline. Standard profiled (clamshell casing) = 1.15x. Built-up (2-piece crown with cap) = 1.30x. Elaborate (3-piece crown with dentil, pilaster surrounds) = 1.60x. Applied per-component type.

quality_effects.notes: Standard residential trim repaint. Spot or full prime (state-dependent) + 2 finish coats satin. Interstage inspection between finish coats but no sanding. 1 interstage cycle (between finish coat 1 and finish coat 2).
Premium trim repaint. Spot or full prime + interstage sand between finish coats (150-grit) + 2 finish coats semi-gloss. 1 interstage cycle. Systematic inspection at 3 ft.

Superior trim repaint. 2-coat primer + interstage sand between ALL coats (180-220 grit) + 2 finish coats gloss. 3 interstage cycles (primer 1->2, primer 2->finish 1, finish 1->finish 2). Raking light inspection at arm's length. Near-zero defect tolerance.

round_configurations.description: Spot prime (bare areas) + 2 finish coats — standard repaint on sound paint
round_configurations.notes: Standard repaint on sound paint. Spot prime bare/thin areas only. Full prime not needed if ASTM D3359 adhesion passes.

round_configurations.description: Spot prime + interstage sand + 2 finish coats — premium on sound paint
round_configurations.notes: Premium trim repaint. Interstage sanding (150-grit) between finish coats. Semi-gloss.

round_configurations.description: 2-coat spot prime + interstage sand between all coats + 2 finish coats — superior
round_configurations.notes: Superior trim repaint. 2-coat primer on bare areas + interstage sand between ALL coats + 2 finish coats gloss. 4 coating passes. Maximum film build and finish quality.
Chalk-binding primer mandatory full coverage. QT4 adds interstage sand between finish coats.

round_configurations.description: 2-coat chalk-binding prime + interstage sand between all + 2 finish coats
round_configurations.notes: Superior on chalking. 2-coat chalk-binding primer + interstage sand between ALL coats + 2 finish coats gloss.

round_configurations.description: Spot prime (bare areas) + 2 finish coats — failing paint <30% bare
round_configurations.notes: Spot prime scraped bare areas. <30% bare does not require full prime. QT4 adds interstage sand. QT5 adds 2-coat spot prime.

round_configurations.description: Full prime + 2 finish coats — failing/peeling >30% bare
round_configurations.notes: Full prime when >30% bare or active peeling. Acrylic stain-block for standard softwood. Alkyd stain-block for tannin-rich (cedar/redwood). QT5 adds 2-coat primer.

round_configurations.description: 2-coat full prime + interstage sand between all + 2 finish coats — severe conditions at QT5
round_configurations.notes: Superior finish on heavily failed trim. 2-coat full primer + interstage sand between ALL coats + 2 finish coats gloss. Maximum coating system.

assumptions: Base rates are for simple flat trim profile at ground access (0-8 ft) on QT3 baseline.
STACKING PARTITION: Prep formula = base_rate / (CONDITION x RRP x HEIGHT x COMPLEXITY). Coating formula = base_rate / (QT x HEIGHT x COMPLEXITY). CONDITION and RRP do NOT stack with QT.

Modifier stacking cap: 4.0x flag threshold. Prep tasks can exceed 4.0x (max theoretical = 14.08x for POOR x RRP x extreme height x elaborate). Coating tasks max = 5.28x (QT5 x extreme x elaborate). Both exceed 4.0x flag — recommend T&M for extreme combinations.
All trim components measured in LF. PCA P10 one-foot rule: trim <12" wide = 1 SF per 1 LF. All production rates expressed as LF/hr.
Brush is primary application method (40 LF/hr baseline). Spray is conditional — justified only for full-house trim volume that amortizes masking overhead.
Spray masking (siding, windows, doors) is a SEPARATE task with its own rate — not combined into spray application rate.
Each trim component processed independently via its own PS key with per-component height and complexity modifiers. Engine sums results across components.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun exposure, surface temp) are NOT estimation modifiers per RC-003 from PaintFactor OS. They are SOP/process concerns.
RRP containment setup/teardown are separate fixed tasks, not rate-modified. The RRP modifier on prep tasks covers only the procedural slowdown (wet methods, HEPA vacuum).
HARD_STOP (DSD-4) is a HARD STOP — triggers scope exclusion, never reaches estimation. Affected components excluded and flagged for carpentry.
QT5 receives 2-coat primer on all substrate states requiring prime, plus interstage sand between ALL coats. This adds significant labor but achieves maximum film build and finish quality.
Caulk tasks use the trim_component_input_group LF inputs. Estimator captures failed caulk LF during condition assessment — not all trim LF has caulk joints.
PVC trim requires bonding primer (not standard acrylic/alkyd). LRV >= 55 or solar-reflective coating gate for dark colors — flagged during color approval, not in estimation.
Crew size = 1 for all tasks. Brush trim work is inherently single-person. Spray may use helper for masking but rate is per painter.

SOP defines several tasks as qt_scaled that were binary in original production.json (scrape, feather_sand, sand_adhesion, caulk_remove_old, caulk_apply, all prime tasks, all finish tasks, chalk_clean). Rates now use qt_rates structure to match SOP task_classification.
TSK_TRRP_FINAL_INSPECT uses FIXED UOM per SOP (not LF as in original production). Qt_scaled via fixed_time_minutes per tier.
Existing production had separate TSK_TRRP_WINDOW_MASK and TSK_TRRP_WINDOW_MASK_SPRAY; SOP consolidates to single TSK_TRRP_PROTECT_WINDOW_GLASS with method-dependent protection_metadata.
Existing production had separate TSK_TRRP_CLEAN_EQUIPMENT_BRUSH and TSK_TRRP_CLEAN_EQUIPMENT_SPRAY; SOP consolidates to single TSK_TRRP_CLEAN_EQUIPMENT.
risks: Prep task modifier stacking on extreme conditions (POOR x RRP x extreme height x elaborate = 14.08x) produces very slow effective rates. Example: heavy scrape at 15 LF/hr base / 12.32 = 1.2 LF/hr effective. CORRECT for 19ft+ ornate trim with severe peeling and lead paint — recommend T&M billing.

Coating task modifier stacking at worst case (QT5 x extreme height x elaborate = 5.28x) produces: brush finish 28 / 5.28 = 5.3 LF/hr effective. This is extreme but correct for gloss finish on elaborate trim at 19ft+.
RRP gate condition adds significant cost beyond the 2.0x prep modifier — containment setup/teardown adds 2-3 hrs per project. Lead test results should be obtained before scoping.
Mixed substrate states on a single building require per-component assessment. One elevation may have sound fascia but peeling casings. Do not average condition across components.

Spray method for trim is SLOWER system rate than brush when including masking time for small-to-medium trim volumes. Only justified for whole-house trim repaint with sufficient LF to amortize masking setup.
PVC trim with LRV <55 paint creates thermal distortion risk. This is a material gate, not an estimation issue — flag and defer to color approval process.
Rot at sills and joints (HARD_STOP) may not be visible until prep begins. Budget for scope change risk on pre-1978 homes with failing paint.

QT5 gloss finish on exterior trim is extremely sensitive to brush marks, dust, and environmental contamination. Production rates at QT5 are significantly slower (1.50x QT modifier) and may require multiple touch-up cycles.
validation_plan: Field-calibrate brush finish rate (40 LF/hr baseline at QT3) on simple flat trim at ground level. Adjust if actual rate differs by >15%.
Validate scraping rates by quality tier — QT3 (35), QT4 (25), QT5 (15) LF/hr. These are the most variable rates in the spec.
Time feather-edge sanding at QT3 (40 LF/hr) on scraped trim profiles. This is a bottleneck task — validate on standard profiled and elaborate profiles separately.
Validate height modifier values by timing identical tasks at ground vs ladder vs scaffold. Target: ground=1.0x, ladder=1.30x, scaffold=1.60x.
Validate complexity modifier by timing brush finish coat on simple flat vs standard profiled vs built-up trim. Target: 1.0x, 1.15x, 1.30x.
Time spray method system rate (spray pass + masking) vs brush method on 200 LF trim section to verify break-even volume for spray justification.
Validate caulk replacement rate (QT3: 50 LF/hr remove, 75 LF/hr apply) on trim joints — includes remove old + clean + apply new. Rate varies significantly by existing caulk type and joint width.
Validate RRP procedural overhead (2.0x on prep) by timing wet scrape vs dry scrape on comparable sections.
Track QT4 vs QT5 interstage sand rates to confirm 60 LF/hr (QT4) and 40 LF/hr (QT5) are realistic for trim profiles.
Field-test condition assessment fixed time (90 min) on projects with 4+ elevations and 6+ component types. Adjust if consistently over/under.
